Workspace execution model
One platform, bounded operating contexts
Overview, My Work, Inbox, Launch, Hiring, Finance, Fundraising, Institution Growth and Individual Growth.
Every record has scope, owner/backup, state, due date, dependency, evidence, reviewer and permitted next action.
Separate designed, implemented, tested, deployed, institution-authorized, production-enabled and native-authoritative.
G01: discovery is not authorization
Walk the complete route-to-runtime chain
1 Inspect the actual router and console mount; #/console is the route mirrored by the inspected prototype, not a new /app/ops implementation claim.
2 Verify account service configuration, signed-in state, active membership and trusted console:operate capability at platform scope.
3 Add/reconcile account-menu discovery only for eligible users; keep denied direct-route behavior intact.
4 Reconcile the workspace catalog and capability/scope filters; Support also depends on its enabled configuration in the inspected prototype.
5 Verify server/RPC, RLS, storage, export and AI boundaries; menu visibility grants no authority.
6 Compare deployed revision/configuration with tested code; test real authorized and denied journeys before accepting G01.
G01 acceptance and diagnostics
Owner: frontend lead | reviewers: platform and trust
No menu: inspect discovery, session and trusted scoped grants. Forbidden route: inspect intended provisioning, not removal of guards.
Missing route: inspect hash routing and registered screen. Empty/blank: inspect configuration, failed queries and runtime errors.
Visible tabs but denied action: trace capability/scope, policy, API/RPC and database decision. Local-only: compare deployment revision and flags.
Tests: signed out denied; student denied; scoped operator allowed; support-disabled hidden; expired/revoked access denied; cross-tenant access denied.
Acceptance requires inspected code references, test outputs, authorized navigation, direct-route denial, correct filters and matching deployment evidence.
G01 discovers the shell. G02 proves data authorization; G03 proves controlled execution. All three are required for an operational launch.

Pilot risk matrix 1
Illustrative likelihood x impact; residual risk requires evidence
R01 Unauthorized disclosure | 3 x 5 = 15 | Trust/platform. Control: Isolation and least privilege. Trigger: Suspected disclosure: contain.
R02 Stale grants/revocation | 3 x 5 = 15 | Platform. Control: Fresh revocation and reconciliation. Trigger: Cannot confirm revoke: deny access.
R03 Duplicate/partial action | 3 x 5 = 15 | Backend. Control: Idempotency and atomic evidence. Trigger: Mismatch: pause commands.
R04 Stale/incorrect data | 4 x 4 = 16 | Integration. Control: Freshness and reconciliation. Trigger: Official mismatch: stop transition.
R05 Absent authority | 3 x 5 = 15 | CEO/counsel/sponsor. Control: Approved scope and agreements. Trigger: Missing approval: no activation.
Pilot risk matrix 2
Illustrative scores are not a measured live assessment
R06 Insufficient coverage | 4 x 4 = 16 | Operations. Control: Backup owners and rehearsal. Trigger: No coverage: defer rollout.
R07 Cash underestimated | 3 x 5 = 15 | Finance/CEO. Control: Reconcile cash and commitments. Trigger: Approved cash floor breached: review spend.
R08 Inaccessible critical task | 3 x 4 = 12 | Design. Control: Manual accessibility validation. Trigger: Critical barrier: block release.
R09 Unsupported claims | 3 x 4 = 12 | CEO/product. Control: Evidence-linked claims review. Trigger: Unverified claim: remove.
R10 Expansion without review | 3 x 5 = 15 | Implementation. Control: New-scope gates. Trigger: Unapproved module/data scope: block expansion.

Institutional acquisition and procurement
Native business workflow from buyer interest to approved agreement
Capture approved lead -> deduplicate account -> assign owner and response clock -> qualify need, sponsor, budget process and timeline.
Discovery -> scope proposal -> implementation feasibility -> pilot success plan -> procurement/security/privacy/accessibility review.
Track procurement requirements, questionnaire answers, evidence versions, reviewers, exceptions, dependencies and expiry; responses cannot overstate readiness.
Quote -> pricing authority -> approved contract versions -> authorized signatures -> executed-document verification -> obligation extraction.
Signature completion starts obligations; it does not automatically authorize tenant activation or official-record authority.
Use bounded signing/payment/identity providers when needed; Semester owns canonical state, approvals, receipts, reconciliation and vendor exit path.
Institutional activation and expansion
Expansion is a new gated scope, not a sales toggle
Executed scope -> tenant setup -> identity configuration -> capabilities -> integration validation -> training -> pilot gates -> authorized cohort.
Success review -> renewal/expansion request -> define new campuses, users, modules, data, costs and authoritative boundaries.
Reassess procurement, security/privacy/accessibility, entitlements, capacity, agreement amendments and institution authority for changed scope.
Approve revised success plan -> controlled configuration -> bounded rollout -> monitor/reconcile -> report verified outcomes.
Expansion is blocked by unresolved critical access/integrity risks, inadequate support capacity, missing authority or unreviewed data scope.
Offboarding: contract/hold review -> export -> final reconciliation -> revoke memberships/credentials -> retention/archive -> closure evidence.
Individual-user acquisition and lifecycle
Student-private work remains separate from institutional records
Discovery -> clear product claims -> account creation/recovery -> policy and consent -> optional plan entitlement -> goal/term onboarding.
First value: create a useful plan/task/course workspace; do not equate signup with activation or an imported plan with an official record.
Return/use -> privacy-preserving service analytics -> user-controlled reminders -> support -> paid upgrade if applicable -> renewal/cancellation.
Institution linking requires verified membership and explicit boundaries; never infer official affiliation or merge private work silently.
Referral/invite workflows are permissioned and consent-aware; no contact scraping, dark patterns or protected educational targeting.
Export/delete requests -> identity verification -> holds/retention -> scoped execution -> receipt; institution-linked records follow their authority.
Native acquisition operating records
Logical entities to reconcile, not automatic new tables
Account, contact/communication preferences, opportunity, procurement review, requirement, evidence version, quote, agreement and document version.
Signature request/receipt, obligation, implementation, tenant, success plan, expansion request, entitlement change and renewal.
Individual journey, activation definition/event, subscription if applicable, consent, support case, rights request and closure receipt.
All state transitions carry scope, owner, current policy, source authority, idempotency, audit correlation, next action and recovery behavior.
Metrics: qualified opportunity conversion, procurement age, signature cycle, launch gate pass rate, first value, support load and renewal; definitions approved before reporting.
Phase-gate decision policy
Proposed review model: GO, CONDITIONAL, NO-GO, PAUSE
GO: all applicable mandatory checks pass with current evidence, named owners and required approvals.
CONDITIONAL: only explicitly permitted noncritical gaps; named remediation owner/date; no waiver of authorization, data integrity or required legal authority.
NO-GO: mandatory missing/failed/stale evidence, inadequate coverage, critical accessibility failure or unapproved scope.
PAUSE: live trigger occurs; contain affected function/cohort, preserve evidence, notify authorized stakeholders and investigate.
Resume requires verified repair, reconciliation, repeat affected tests and renewed approval when scope or risk changed.
Tracker completeness is not readiness. Independent release, institution and authoritative-domain gates remain separate.
Hiring pipeline
Planning roles, not approved headcount
Prioritize platform/backend capacity, then pilot implementation/operations coverage; obtain fractional counsel and trust/accessibility review as required.
Requisition -> workload justification -> affordability -> scorecard -> structured assessment -> approved offer -> IP/agreement -> scoped access -> training.
Do not enter sensitive candidate data into the local workspace. Production hiring needs restricted records and retention controls.
Investor fundraising tracker
No invented investors, funding ask or commitments
Research -> qualified -> introduction -> meeting -> follow-up -> diligence -> nonbinding interest -> definitive documents -> funds received.
Track owner, next action/date, approved deck version, diligence asks, authority and outcome.
Days 1-30: reconcile capital needs; Days 31-60: approve deck/data room; Days 61-90: authorized outreach and diligence.
Signing interest is not cash. External outreach and sharing require approval.
Operations Inbox
Canonical events, not a parallel ticket database
Queues: approvals, escalations, incidents, renewals, data requests, security alerts and lead response obligations.
Ingest -> deduplicate -> scope -> assign -> approved clock -> triage -> controlled action -> receipt -> verify -> resolve/escalate.
Define business/elapsed time, timezone, pauses, reopening and escalation; no contractual SLA is invented.
